message.content:
Taro chips fried, seasoned: classification options include 2008.99 (fruits, nuts, other edible parts of plants, prepared or preserved, not elsewhere specified) or 2005.99 (other vegetables prepared or preserved otherwise than by vinegar, not frozen). Taro is a root vegetable, but CBP rulings on taro chips have classified them under 2005.99.9700 (other vegetables, other: other), which is the usual outcome for potato-chip-like products from vegetables other than potatoes. Potato chips go to 2005.20.

Note that 2005.99.97 is the "Other" within the 2005.99.9 subheading, while 2005.99.80 covers "Other" under 2005.99.80 (Other: ...). Checking, the 2005.99 subheadings: 2005.99.10 (Chicory), 2005.99.20 (Artichokes, etc.), 2005.99.40 (Cabbage?), 2005.99.50 (Sauerkraut), 2005.99.60 (Capers/olives), 2005.99.80 (Other: Kimchi?), and 2005.99.9100 (Pickled vegetables), 2005.99.9200 (Mixtures), 2005.99.9400 (Garlic), 2005.99.9700 (Other). Taro chips are usually placed in 2005.99.9700.

{"hts_code": "2005.99.9700", "reason": "Fried, seasoned taro root slices are a vegetable prepared or preserved otherwise than by vinegar, not frozen, and fall in the residual 2005.99 provision for other vegetables."}
